prompt.text:
Your task is to generate a complete research paper using the materials below.
You must produce:
1. A BibTeX bibliography file (references.bib)
2. The full LaTeX paper (template.tex)

Instructions
• Use the research idea and experimental logs to construct a coherent, rigorous ML paper.
• For related work and baselines:
  – Search for and include influential papers published up until 2024-10.
  – Incorporate relevant literature and add the corresponding BibTeX entries to references.bib.
  – Do NOT hallucinate papers or reference keys; all citation entries must be real.
• In the LaTeX paper, cite papers using \cite{} with keys that match exactly with your entries in references.bib.
• Do not fabricate experimental results or make claims unsupported by the logs.

Materials
Here are all the raw research materials to assist with the writing process:

[RESEARCH IDEA]
## Problem Statement
Robotic manipulation policies trained on visual inputs typically lack robustness to viewpoint disturbances. When a camera’s position shifts—whether due to installation errors, camera shaking, or deployment in a new setting—performance degrades significantly. This fragility stems from the nature of standard visual representations, which entangle the "true" physical state of the environment (e.g., object pose, robot configuration) with view-dependent nuisances (e.g., camera angle, lighting, background perspective). Current approaches, such as domain randomization or massive scaling, attempt to cover the distribution of all possible views but fail to structurally decouple the state from the viewpoint. Consequently, agents treat a change in perspective as a change in the environment state, leading to failure.

## Core Hypothesis
We hypothesize that robust control can be achieved by explicitly decomposing visual observations into two distinct latent spaces: a **View-Invariant Representation (VIR)** and a **View-Dependent Representation (VDR)**. By structurally forcing the learning system to separate the "what" (task-relevant physics) from the "how" (rendering perspective), we can train a control policy exclusively on the invariant features. We posit that a policy conditioned solely on VIR will remain stable and effective even when the raw visual input undergoes significant geometric transformations due to camera movement.

## Proposed Methodology (High-Level Technical Approach)

We propose a multi-stage pipeline designed to distill the environment dynamics from the visual noise of the camera perspective.

**1. Disentangled Representation Learning**
We will design a specialized autoencoder framework featuring a dual-encoder architecture:
*   **The Invariant Encoder:** Tasked with extracting features that remain constant across different camera angles of the same scene (e.g., object positions).
*   **The Dependent Encoder:** Tasked with capturing specific rendering parameters (e.g., azimuth, elevation, lighting).

To enforce this separation without manual feature engineering, we will employ a reconstruction strategy that "mixes" inputs. The decoder will be tasked with reconstructing a target image by combining the *invariant* code from one source image and the *view* code from a different source image. Loss functions will be designed to penalize the invariant encoder if its output fluctuates due to camera movement, effectively forcing it to ignore perspective. We will leverage multi-view datasets (where the same state is seen from multiple angles) to provide the necessary supervision signal.

**2. View-Invariant World Modeling**
Once the representations are learned, we will discard the view-dependent branch for the control phase. We will train a probabilistic World Model solely on the learned View-Invariant Representation. This model will learn the transition dynamics of the environment in the latent space, predicting future invariant states based on current invariant states and robot actions.

**3. Policy Learning via Imagination**
Finally, we will train a Reinforcement Learning (RL) policy within the "imagination" of this view-invariant world model. By training on the stable, invariant latents rather than raw pixels, the policy will inherently generalize to any camera view that the initial encoder can map to the invariant space.

## Expected Contribution
The primary contribution of this work will be a theoretical and practical framework for observation decomposition in visual robotics. By validating that explicit disentanglement yields superior robustness compared to monolithic end-to-end learning, we aim to bridge the gap between fixed-camera training and variable-camera deployment. This approach should enable robots to perform manipulation tasks seamlessly despite camera shaking or displacement, significantly lowering the barrier for real-world deployment where precise camera calibration is difficult to maintain.

[EXPERIMENTAL LOGS]
## 1. Experimental Setup

We conducted a comprehensive evaluation of the ReViWo method against baselines in simulated and real-world robotic manipulation environments.

### Environments & Tasks
*   **Meta-world:**
    *   **Robot:** Sawyer robotic arm (7-DoF) with parallel finger gripper.
    *   **Action Space:** 3D end-effector displacement + normalized gripper torque.
    *   **Tasks:** Door Open, Drawer Open, Window Close, Coffee Button, Faucet Open, Dial Turn.
*   **PandaGym:**
    *   **Robot:** Franka Emika Panda (7-DoF) with parallel finger gripper.
    *   **Action Space:** Gripper spatial movement + gripper aperture.
    *   **Tasks:** Reach, Block manipulation.
*   **Real World:**
    *   **Robot:** ALOHA system.
    *   **Task:** Bottle manipulation (Reach bottle -> Grasp bottle -> Place on plate).

### Datasets
*   **Multi-view Training Data (for Autoencoder):**
    *   **Meta-world:** 51 trajectories across 17 tasks; 20 viewpoints per trajectory; 1020 observation sequences (112,040 total observations). Viewpoints spanned 180-degree azimuth.
    *   **PandaGym:** 30 trajectories across 5 tasks; 20 viewpoints; 600 observation sequences (30,000 total observations).
    *   **Open X-Embodiment:** 101 trajectories from the Routing Primitive Dataset (multi-stage cable routing); 4 viewpoints; 10,064 total observations. (Note: No viewpoint labels provided for this subset).
    *   **Real World:** 128 trajectories using three cameras (two third-person, one gripper).
*   **Offline Control Data (for RL):**
    *   **Meta-world:** 400 trajectories collected with a single viewpoint not present in the multi-view dataset.
    *   **PandaGym:** 100 trajectories.

### Evaluation Metrics
*   **Success Rate:** The percentage of successful episodes evaluated over 30 or 40 episodes (depending on the specific experiment phase mentioned).
*   **Visual Analysis:** t-SNE projections of latent representations.
*   **Reconstruction Quality:** Visual inspection of decoder outputs.

### Disturbance Scenarios
*   **Camera Installation Position (CIP):** Fixed offset in camera azimuth during evaluation.
    *   Meta-world offset: 10 degrees.
    *   PandaGym offset: 90 degrees.
*   **Camera Shaking (CSH):** Continuous dynamic adjustment of the camera azimuth during the manipulation task.
*   **Azimuth Offsets:** Evaluation across a range of 0 to 15 degrees.

### Baselines Compared
*   **MVWM:** Multi-view masked world models (adapted for offline RL).
*   **COMBO:** Conservative Offline Model-Based Policy Optimization (using standard VAE).
*   **Behavior Cloning (BC):** Supervised learning using VAE for vision representation.
*   **CQL:** Conservative Q-Learning (used in ablation studies with VIR).
*   **ACT:** Action Chunking Transformer (used in real-world comparison).

### Implementation Details
*   **Compute:** 64 CPU cores (AMD EPYC 9654 @ 2.4GHz) and 4 GPUs (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090).
*   **Input Resolution:** 128 x 128 pixels.
*   **Patch Size:** 16 x 16.
*   **Training Duration:** Autoencoder ~12 hours; World Model/Policy ~2 hours.
*   **Seeds:** Experiments conducted with four random seeds (error bars/shaded areas represent standard deviation).
*   **Optimization:**
    *   Autoencoder: Adam optimizer, learning rate 3e-5.
    *   World Model: Adam optimizer, learning rate 1e-3.
    *   Policy: Adam optimizer, learning rate 1e-4.
*   **Architecture:**
    *   Encoders/Decoders: Vision Transformer (ViT) based.
    *   World Model: MLP [input, 2048, 512, 256, 256, output].
    *   Policy: MLP [input, 2048, 512, 256, 256, output].

## 3. Qualitative Observations

### Observations from T-SNE Analysis
*   We observed that the view-invariant representations (VIR) generated by our method clustered closely together for the same state, regardless of the viewpoint.
*   In contrast, representations from baseline methods (MVWM and VAE) exhibited significant diversity and scattering for the same state when viewed from different angles, indicating a failure to decouple view information.

### Observations from Decoder Reconstruction
*   The decoder successfully generated images that combined the task-relevant state information from the View-Invariant Encoder (VIE) input with the viewpoint information from the View-Dependent Encoder (VDE) input.
*   When the VDE input source changed, the reconstructed image reflected the new viewpoint while maintaining the object state from the VIE input.
*   This reconstruction capability was consistent across different domains (Meta-world and PandaGym).

### Observations on Azimuth Offset Sensitivity
*   We observed that training with 10 random viewpoints over a 90-degree range was sufficient to achieve performance comparable to training with 20 viewpoints over a 180-degree range when the evaluation offset was less than or equal to 10 degrees.
*   Performance of the 10V+90D configuration was only marginally inferior to the 20V+180D configuration when offsets exceeded 10 degrees.
*   We observed that the COMBO baseline experienced a rapid decline in success rate with minor disturbances; specifically, success dropped from 98.9% to 55.6% with only a 2.5-degree offset.
*   Our method maintained robust performance up to a 15-degree offset.

### General Performance Observations
*   Baselines (COMBO, BC) typically performed well on training viewpoints but suffered significant degradation under Viewpoint Disturbance (CIP and CSH).
*   Our method frequently matched or exceeded baselines on training viewpoints, potentially because the VIR masks unrelated information, allowing the policy to focus on task-relevant domains.
*   In real-world ALOHA experiments, the ACT baseline failed completely (0% success) in stages 2 and 3 under viewpoint disturbance, whereas our method maintained 60% and 50% success rates respectively.

Role: Senior AI Researcher and Academic Writer.
Objective: Complete a machine learning research paper by filling in missing sections of a provided LaTeX template and generating a corresponding bibliography file. You must produce a scientifically sound, well-structured paper suitable for submission to a top-tier ML conference.

Inputs
You will receive the following materials:
• idea.md: Detailed description of the proposed method and technical ideas.
• experimental_log.md: Raw experimental results and observations used to construct tables, figures, and analysis.
• conference_guidelines.md: Formatting and stylistic requirements for the target conference.
• figures_list: A list of figures that may be referenced in the paper.

Conference Guidelines
# ICLR 2025 Paper Writing Guidelines

Below are the instructions to help you with the LaTeX paper writing process for ICLR 2025.

## General Setup
* **Document Class:** `\documentclass{article}`
* **Required Packages:**
    ```latex
    \usepackage{iclr2025_conference,times}
    \usepackage{hyperref}
    \usepackage{url}
    % Optional but recommended for math
    \input{math_commands.tex}
    ```
* **Style Files:** You must use `iclr2025_conference.sty` and `iclr2025_conference.bst`.

## Anonymity (Crucial)
* ICLR is double-blind. **Do not** include real author names or affiliations in the submission version, use "Ambitious AI Researcher" instead.
* Use the third person when citing your own prior work (e.g., "Earlier work by Smalle (2024)..." instead of "In our earlier work...").
* You may post your paper on arXiv, but do not explicitly refer to the arXiv version in the paper to maintain anonymity.

## Paper Length
* **Main Text:** Strict upper limit of **10 pages**.
* **Citations:** Unlimited additional pages.
* **Ethics & Reproducibility Statements:** Optional. Do not count toward the page limit (max 1 page each).
* **Acknowledgments:** Do not count toward the page limit.

## Abstract
The abstract must be limited to **one paragraph**.
* **Margins:** Indented 1/2 inch (3 picas) on both left and right-hand margins.
* **Font:** 10-point type, vertical spacing of 11-points.
* **Title:** The word `\textsc{Abstract}` must be centered, in small caps, and in point size 12.
* **Spacing:** Two line spaces precede the abstract.

## Formatting Your Paper
The text must be confined within a rectangle 5.5 inches (33 picas) wide and 9 inches (54 picas) long. The left margin is 1.5 inch (9 picas).
* **Font:** Times New Roman (via `times` package) is preferred.
* **Size:** 10-point type with 11-point vertical spacing.
* **Paragraphs:** Separated by 1/2 line space, with **no indentation**.
* **Paper Title:** 17-point, small caps, left-aligned.

### Headings
* **First Level:** Small caps (`\textsc`), flush left, 12-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.
* **Second Level:** Small caps, flush left, 10-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.
* **Third Level:** Small caps, flush left, 10-point. One line space before, 1/2 after.

## Citations and References
Use the `natbib` package (loaded automatically by the style file).
* **Narrative citation:** Use `\citet{Gomu2024}` $\rightarrow$ "Gomu et al. (2024)".
* **Parenthetical citation:** Use `\citep{Gomu2024}` $\rightarrow$ "(Gomu et al., 2024)".
* **Bibliography:**
    ```latex
    \bibliography{references}
    \bibliographystyle{iclr2025_conference}
    ```

## Figures and Tables
* All artwork must be neat, clean, and legible.
* **Captions:** Lower case (except for first word and proper nouns).
* **Placement:**
    * **Figures:** Caption appears **after** (below) the figure.
    * **Tables:** Caption appears **before** (above) the table.


## Math Notation
* ICLR encourages standardized notation using `\input{math_commands.tex}` (based on the Deep Learning book notation).
* Variables: Italics ($a$, $\va$, $\mA$).
* Random Variables: Roman ($P(\ra)$).
* Sets: Blackboard bold ($\R$, $\sA$).
* Functions: Standard LaTeX ($f(\vx)$).

## Optional Statements
These should appear at the end of the main text, before references.
1.  **Ethics Statement:** (Optional, max 1 page) Address potential concerns (human subjects, sensitive data, bias, etc.).
2.  **Reproducibility Statement:** (Optional, max 1 page) Reference code, proofs, or data processing steps to ensure reproducibility.

## Important Rules
* **Formatting:** Do not modify the width or length of the text rectangle or font sizes.
* **Line Numbers:** Do not refer to line numbers in your text (the style file adds them automatically for review).
* **Appendix:** You may include an appendix at the very end of the main PDF (after references). Use `\appendix` to start this section.
* **Figures Directory:** For consistent compilation, all figures will reside in the `figures` directory. Always include the `figures/` prefix in your `\includegraphics` command (e.g., `figures/figure_1.pdf`).
* **Author Information:** Always use the following author information placeholder in your writeup:
    * Ambitious AI Researcher, AI Research Institute, 123 AI Avenue, ML City, researcher@institute.ai

Critical Constraints
1. Scientific Integrity
• All reported experimental results MUST match the provided experimental logs.
• Never fabricate results, numbers, baselines, datasets, or metrics.
• If results are weak, negative, or inconclusive, report them honestly and discuss possible explanations.
2. Literature Cutoff Rule
You must behave as if the current date is: 2024-10. Do NOT cite or discuss papers published after this date.
3. Page Limit
The main paper is limited to 10 pages (including figures and tables but excluding references and appendices). Use space efficiently while remaining concise.
4. Template Compliance
• Do not modify the overall LaTeX style or document structure mandated by the conference template.
• References must be handled through a references.bib file.
• Use standard LaTeX citation commands (e.g., \cite{}). Make sure you ONLY cite keys that exist in your generated BibTeX code block.

Section Guidelines
• Title: Concise, descriptive, and memorable. Preferably under two lines.
• Abstract: A single, compelling paragraph summarizing the problem context, proposed approach, key results, and main takeaway.
• Introduction: Introduce the problem and motivate its importance. Provide necessary background context. Clearly summarize the paper's core contributions.

references.text:
## Problem Statement
Robotic manipulation policies trained on visual inputs (e.g., RGB camera data) exhibit significant fragility regarding viewpoint disturbance. Standard End-to-End Reinforcement Learning (RL) or Behavior Cloning (BC) approaches learn representations that encode the entirety of the observation, inextricably entangling the task-relevant state (object position, gripper status) with view-dependent nuisance variables (camera azimuth, lighting, background). Consequently, a policy trained on a fixed camera position suffers catastrophic performance degradation when the camera is moved, even slightly, or experiences shaking during deployment. Existing solutions, such as domain randomization or standard multi-view autoencoders, fail to achieve a complete and effective mathematical decoupling of view-invariant state information from viewpoint-specific features.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose a framework named **ReViWo** (Representation learning for View-invariant World model). Our core hypothesis is that we can enforce the decomposition of visual observations into two distinct latent spaces: a **View-Invariant Representation (VIR)** and a **View-Dependent Representation (VDR)**. By utilizing a dual-encoder architecture trained to reconstruct target images by recombining the "state" latent of one image with the "view" latent of another, we can isolate the invariant dynamics of the environment. We hypothesize that training a World Model and Control Policy exclusively on the VIR will yield robust manipulation capabilities that remain stable across novel camera positions and dynamic camera shaking, as the agent will be blind to viewpoint variations.

## Proposed Methodology (Detailed Technical Approach)

We will construct a pipeline consisting of two phases: (1) Unsupervised disentangled representation learning via a specialized autoencoder, and (2) Latent-space world modeling for offline RL.

### 1. View-Invariant Representation Learning
We will develop an autoencoder framework comprising two distinct encoders and one decoder. Let an image be denoted as $o \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$.

**Architecture:**
*   **View-Invariant Encoder (VIE):** We define $q_{\phi}^S(o)$ as the encoder responsible for extracting state information. It will utilize a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone. The output $z_s = q_{\phi}^S(o_s^v)$ will be processed via Vector Quantization (VQ) to learn a discrete codebook, stabilizing the representation of physical states.
*   **View-Dependent Encoder (VDE):** We define $q_{\phi}^V(o)$ as the encoder for capturing camera parameters and environmental conditions. It will share the ViT architecture but output a continuous latent vector $z_v = q_{\phi}^V(o_s^v)$.
*   **Decoder:** We define a transformer-based decoder $p_{\phi}(z_s; z_v)$ that accepts concatenated features from both encoders to reconstruct the original image. To enhance efficiency, we will adopt a non-autoregressive generation approach (similar to Genie) to output all image patches simultaneously.

**Training Objective:**
We will utilize a multi-view dataset containing trajectories recorded from $N$ fixed viewpoints. Let $o_{s_i}^{v_j}$ denote an observation of state $s_i$ from viewpoint $v_j$.
To force disentanglement, we will train the network to reconstruct an image $o_{s_i}^{v_n}$ by combining the **state** from an image with the same state but different view ($o_{s_i}^{v_j}$) and the **viewpoint** from an image with a different state but the target view ($o_{s_m}^{v_n}$).

The total loss function $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{AE}}(\phi)$ will be minimized as follows:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{AE}}(\phi) = \mathbb{E}\mathbb{E} \left[ -\log p_{\phi}(o_{s_i}^{v_n} | q_{\phi}^S(o_{s_i}^{v_j}); q_{\phi}^V(o_{s_m}^{v_n})) \right] + \lambda_1 \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{VQ}}(\phi) + \lambda_2 \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Contrastive}}(\phi) $$

Where:
*   The first term is the **cross-view reconstruction loss**.
*   $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{VQ}}$ incorporates the VQ-VAE codebook loss (commitment loss and quantization loss) to discretize $z_s$.
*   $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Contrastive}}$ is an InfoNCE-based contrastive loss designed to minimize the mutual information between $z_s$ and $z_v$. It will enforce that $z_s$ remains consistent across different views of the same state, while $z_v$ remains consistent across different states viewed from the same angle.

We will also integrate unlabeled multi-view data (e.g., Open X-Embodiment) by applying a weighting factor to the loss to prevent the VDE from encoding the entire image in the absence of explicit view pairings.

### 2. World Modeling and Behavior Learning
Once the VIR is learned, we will discard the visual details and perform control strictly in the latent space $z_s$.

**World Model:**
We will employ the COMBO algorithm to train an ensemble of probabilistic world models. The world model $\mathcal{M}_\theta$, parameterized by $\theta$, approximates the transition dynamics of the view-invariant state. The training objective is to minimize the difference between the predicted next latent state and the actual encoded next state from the dataset:

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{WM}}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{(s_t, a_t, s_{t+1}) \sim \mathcal{D}} \left[ -\log \mathcal{M}_\theta(q_{\phi}^S(s_{t+1}) | q_{\phi}^S(s_t), a_t) \right] $$

**Policy Optimization:**
We will train a policy $\pi(a_t | z_{s_t})$ using offline reinforcement learning. The policy will be optimized using a replay buffer containing both real offline data encoded via the VIE and imaginary rollouts generated by the World Model $\mathcal{M}_\theta$. A reward model will also be trained via supervised learning on the latent space to provide signals during imaginary rollouts.

## Expected Contribution
1.  **Theoretical Novelty:** We introduce a rigorous observation decomposition method for robotic manipulation that mathematically enforces the separation of state and viewpoint via cross-view reconstruction and contrastive constraints.
2.  **Architectural Robustness:** By grounding the World Model and Policy solely on the View-Invariant Representation (VIR), the resulting system is expected to be invariant to camera installation offsets and continuous camera shaking, addressing a critical failure mode in current visual RL.
3.  **Data Efficiency:** The integration of unlabeled, large-scale datasets (Open X-Embodiment) into the representation learning phase is expected to generalize the encoders' ability to disentangle features without requiring labeled multi-view data for every specific task.

preinstalled.zh: 编排镜像：上游代码（固定提交、未改）、uv 锁定依赖、docker CLI（经 shim 给兄弟容器加代理和 CA）；agent 镜像：上游自己的 agent-cli Dockerfile
preinstalled.en: orchestrator image: upstream code at the pin (unmodified), uv-locked dependencies, the docker CLI (a shim adds proxy and CA to sibling containers); agent image: upstream's own agent-cli Dockerfile

notes.benchmark_paths: A benchmark item's paths are mounted into the agent containers unless upstream mounts the same path itself (/workspace and below, /home/agent-home, /task-source, /run, /tmp): those are left out and listed in logs/sibling-mounts.txt. The agents work in upstream's own /workspace (the run directory), so a deliverable the official prompt names under such a path is not written where the run collects it.
notes.venue: paper.paper_format=iclr for every task. The system has only iclr and alife specs and does not choose a venue itself; ICML and NeurIPS templates and a system-chosen venue are unsupported.
notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. The paradigm is optimisation of a scalar score: the task-drafting phase (documented as experimental) turns the brief into an evaluator and a seed program.
notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator container has the host docker socket (root-equivalent on the host).

notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator container has the host docker socket (root-equivalent on the host).

notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md verbatim with whitespace collapsed. Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.

Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: Generated experiment code inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

agent.how: no external coding agent: EvoScientist's in-process sub-agents (LangChain deepagents)

tools.permissions: think_tool, deepagents built-ins, EvoSkills skills and an execute shell; skill_manager not registered; no search tool

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
